transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brought me in is... people keep saying I’m not listening to them. Like, my supervisor at the plant or my wife, they'll be talking straight to me, and... actually, my supervisor, Dave, he was just on my case about this on Tuesday. Or maybe Wednesday? I think it was Wednesday because the main conveyor belt got jammed up again. We've been telling maintenance to fix that belt for three weeks, and they just keep patching it with this cheap rubber. It’s ridiculous, honestly, you can't run a line like that. 

But anyway, he’ll be standing right in front of my face talking, or my wife will be telling me something at home, and a minute later I just... I realize I only caught half of it. I end up having to ask them to say the whole thing again. Which really drives my wife crazy, especially if she's talking about her sister. Her sister just bought this house out in the county and the plumbing is a total nightmare. I told her she needed a better inspector before she signed the papers, but... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, yeah. I just keep missing what people are saying.
Do you find that your mind is elsewhere when people are talking to you, or are you just having trouble focusing on what they're saying?

I'm not really sure what the difference is, to be honest. It’s like... I’m looking right at them, but my brain is already out in the parking lot. Like, I’ll be standing there and suddenly I’m thinking about my truck. The transmission has been slipping in second gear, and I just know if I take it to that shop down on 4th street, they're gonna try to upcharge me for a whole rebuild. 

Those guys are absolute crooks. They charged my buddy Steve eight hundred bucks just for a water pump on his Chevy. Eight hundred! And Steve was telling me I should just buy the parts online and we could do it in his driveway, but his driveway is on this really steep hill, so you can't exactly jack a heavy truck up safely on that... you know, it's just asking for it to roll off the stands and crush somebody. 

But yeah, wait. Sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, focusing. Yeah, I guess my mind just completely takes off somewhere else.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

Yeah, constantly. Like, if I’m sitting in one of our morning safety huddles at the plant, my leg is just bouncing a mile a minute. I’ll be messing with a pen or jingling my keys without even realizing it, and the guys next to me will actually tell me to knock it off because I’m shaking the whole bench. 

Which, honestly, those benches are incredibly flimsy anyway. Management bought them from some surplus catalog a couple years ago, and I swear the bolts are already rusting out. I told maintenance they need to put some Loctite on the threads or somebody is gonna sit down and the whole thing is gonna collapse. You know, they never listen to us guys on the floor. It's like they think we don't know how basic hardware works. The plant manager, Mr. Henderson, he doesn't even know how the machinery runs, but he drives this brand new BMW and parks it right in the fire lane... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Sitting still. Yeah, same thing at the dinner table at home. My leg is just going and going, shaking the table until my wife puts her hand on my knee to get me to stop. I just can't seem to turn the motor off.
Do you have difficulty completing tasks or projects because you lose interest or get distracted?

Tasks? Nah, I wouldn't say that. I don't really have trouble finishing things. If I start a project, I get it done. 

Take last weekend, I was pulling apart the carburetor on my push mower. It's an older Toro, great machine, but the ethanol in the gas they sell now just completely eats through the rubber seals. You really gotta buy that premium non-oxygenated stuff if you want your small engines to last. I was actually just telling my neighbor, Bill, about that because his weed whacker wouldn't start. Bill's a nice guy, but he leaves all his tools out in the weather. I saw his good DeWalt drill just sitting on his patio table through that whole thunderstorm we had on Sunday. 

I mean, those lithium batteries are not cheap. If you short out a 20-volt max battery, you're looking at ninety, maybe a hundred bucks to replace it at Home Depot. And they lock them up in those plastic cages now, so you have to track down an employee just to buy one, and you can never find anybody working in the hardware aisle. They always have like one guy covering three departments... 

Wait, what was the question? Something about projects? Yeah, no, I don't lose interest. I finish what I start.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Impulse? No, I don't think so. I'm pretty careful about stuff. I mean, I don't just do things without thinking. 

Like at the plant, safety is a huge deal. You can't just go pressing buttons on the stamping press without checking the line first. We had a guy last year, new kid, probably fresh out of high school, and he didn't lock out the machine before reaching in to clear a jam. He didn't get hurt, thank God, but the safety manager was screaming at him so loud you could hear it over the machinery. And that guy, the safety manager, he takes his job way too seriously. He walks around with this clipboard, acting like he's a cop or something. Last week he tried to write me up because my safety glasses were on top of my head while I was walking to the break room. The break room! There's nothing flying around in there except maybe the stale donuts from the day shift. 

And don't even get me started on the coffee in that break room. It's like drinking battery acid. They buy these massive tubs of the cheapest grounds they can find, and the filter is always overflowing. I keep telling them we should all just chip in five bucks a month and get a Keurig, but nobody wants to organize it. I might just bring my own thermos from home, honestly. My wife got me this really nice Stanley one for Christmas, the classic green one, keeps coffee hot for like fourteen hours...

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Acting on impulse? No, I wouldn't say I do that. I'm pretty careful.
When did you first notice that you were having trouble paying attention to what people were saying?

Paying attention? Well, I guess it's really been a problem for about two years and two months now. That's when my wife, Sarah, went back to work outside the house. She got this job at the dental clinic downtown, doing the front desk stuff. Which is great for her, you know, she needed to get out of the house. But man, the parking downtown is an absolute nightmare. They expect her to pay twenty dollars a day just to park in the garage next door, which completely eats into what she's making. I told her she should just park at the grocery store a few blocks away and walk, but she says they tow if you leave it there all day. 

And those tow truck guys, they are like vultures. I swear they just sit in the alley waiting for someone to walk away from their car. My buddy Dave had his truck towed from that exact lot last year. He was just running in to grab a sandwich at the deli across the street, gone for maybe ten minutes, and when he came back, his truck was gone. Cost him three hundred bucks to get it out of the impound, and they scratched his bumper. He tried to fight it, called the city and everything, but you know how that goes. You can never get a real person on the phone, just those automated menus that just loop you back to the beginning... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, paying attention. Yeah, so since Sarah started working, I've had to handle a lot more of the schedule on my own, like the kids' stuff and the house stuff, and that's when I really noticed I just can't keep track of what people are telling me. It's just been really bad since then.
Did you have trouble paying attention or sitting still when you were a kid, before you turned 12?

Sitting still? Yeah, I was like this even as a kid. My teachers were always moving my seat because I couldn't stay put, and I was always getting into trouble for calling out answers or butting into other kids' work. This was all way before middle school. 

I remember in third grade, Mrs. Gable's class, she moved my desk right up next to hers. She was this older lady, always wore these thick wool sweaters even when it was warm out. She had this weird smell, kind of like mothballs and peppermint. Actually, my grandmother used to smell exactly like that. She lived in this old farmhouse out in the country, and she kept peppermint candies in this little crystal dish on the coffee table. The candies were always stuck together, so you had to pry them apart, and sometimes you'd get little shards of crystal stuck to them. 

That farmhouse was amazing, though. It had this huge wrap-around porch, and we used to catch fireflies in mason jars out there in the summer. My cousin Jimmy and I would stay out until it was pitch black. Jimmy's a mechanic now, actually, down in Texas. Works on those massive diesel rigs. He makes really good money, but the heat down there is just brutal. I went to visit him a couple of years ago in August, and I swear the asphalt was melting my shoes. You couldn't even touch the steering wheel in his truck without burning your hands...

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about being a kid? Oh, yeah, sitting still. No, I couldn't sit still at all back then. Always getting in trouble for it.
Do you ever find yourself so focused on something that you tune out everything else around you?

Focusing on something? No, I don't really get like that. I'm usually pretty aware of what's going on around me. I don't really tune things out. 

Actually, speaking of tuning things out, my neighbor's dog has been barking non-stop for the last three days. It's this little yappy terrier thing, and they just leave it out in the yard while they're at work. I tried talking to them about it, but the guy, he's a real piece of work. He's got this huge boat parked in his driveway that he hasn't moved in five years. It's taking up half the space, and the cover is all torn up and flapping in the wind. I don't even know why you'd buy a boat if you live this far from the lake. The closest marina is at least a two-hour drive, and that's if you don't hit traffic on I-95. 

Traffic on 95 is getting worse every year, I swear. They've been doing construction on the overpass near my exit for what feels like a decade. They put up all those orange barrels and then you never see anyone actually working. Just miles of brake lights. I tried taking the back roads last week to avoid it, but everyone else had the same idea, so I ended up stuck behind a garbage truck doing twenty miles an hour. And the smell! It was garbage day in that neighborhood, so all the cans were out, and the truck was just leaking this gross liquid onto the street...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about the dog? No, wait, focusing. Yeah, no, I don't really get hyper-focused on stuff like that. I'm always kind of bouncing around.
Were you more active or restless than your siblings or friends when you were a kid?

More active than my brother? Oh, man, night and day. He could just sit on the rug for hours watching cartoons or building blocks, but me? If I have to sit still, it literally feels like this huge pressure building up inside my chest and my legs. Like I’ve got to move or do something right now or I’ll just crawl out of my skin. 

Actually, pressure building up... it's exactly like the hydraulic presses down at the plant. I work on the production line, and we've got these massive machines that stamp out metal casings. When the pressure valve gets stuck on one of them, it makes this awful, high-pitched whining noise that drives everybody insane. Last Tuesday, the new guy, Kevin—he's only been there a month, nice kid but doesn't know a wrench from a screwdriver—he thought he could fix it by just whacking the side of the machine with a rubber mallet. I yelled at him, I said, "Hey, you're gonna blow a seal doing that!" But he did it anyway, and sure enough, hydraulic fluid sprayed everywhere. It took the maintenance guys four hours to clean it up. They had to use that gritty sawdust stuff to soak it up, you know? It smells like fake oranges. My high school janitor used to use that exact same stuff whenever some kid threw up in the hallway. God, I hated high school. The cafeteria always smelled like that orange stuff mixed with stale tater tots...

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my brother and friends. Yeah, they were all real calm, but I just couldn't do it. I just always had that pressure, always had to be moving around.
Do you think your trouble paying attention is more of a problem for you than your restlessness and fidgeting?

Trouble paying attention? No, I don't really think so. The paying attention part isn't really the issue for me. It's the... the restlessness, the always having to be doing something. That's what really gets me. 

Like, if I'm just sitting there, my legs start bouncing, my hands start tapping. It's like I have a motor running inside me that won't shut off. Speaking of motors, my buddy Dave just bought this vintage Mustang. Beautiful car, cherry red, 1968. He's been restoring it in his garage for the last three years. I go over there sometimes on weekends to help him out. We were trying to tune the carburetor last Sunday, and man, those old Holleys can be tricky. You get the air-fuel mixture just a tiny bit off, and the whole thing runs rough. Dave's got this whole setup in his garage, too. He's got a mini-fridge stocked with beer, a big screen TV mounted on the wall. He even put down that epoxy coating on the floor. It looks like a showroom in there. 

I was thinking about doing that to my garage, actually. The concrete is all stained from where my old truck used to leak oil. That truck was a nightmare. I bought it off this guy on Craigslist, and he swore up and down it ran great. Two weeks later, the transmission slips. I had to replace the whole thing. Cost me a fortune. And the guy, of course, stopped answering my calls. You really can't trust people on the internet these days. Everybody's trying to make a quick buck. It's like that time I bought concert tickets online and they turned out to be fake...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about the fidgeting? Yeah, the fidgeting and the restlessness, that's definitely the bigger problem. The attention stuff, I don't really notice that as much. It's just the moving. I can't stop moving.
Did your trouble with restlessness and fidgeting start before you were 12 years old?

Yeah, oh yeah, definitely before I was 12. I was exactly like this even as a little kid. I remember my teachers were always moving my seat around the classroom because I just couldn't stay put. I was always jumping up, calling out answers before they even finished asking the question, and I was always getting into trouble for butting into other kids' work. This was way before middle school. 

Speaking of middle school, they tore down my old middle school last year to build a strip mall. Can you believe that? A strip mall. Like we need another place to buy cheap cell phone cases and over-priced smoothies. I drove by the construction site a couple weeks ago, and they've got this massive crane set up. It’s one of those tower cranes, you know? The ones they use for skyscrapers. My uncle used to operate one of those down in the city. He said the wind up there is crazy. You sit in this tiny little glass box hundreds of feet in the air, and the whole thing just sways back and forth. He said he had to bring a thermos of coffee with him every morning because if he had to go to the bathroom, it took him twenty minutes just to climb down the ladder. 

I don't know how anybody drinks that much coffee anyway. I had two cups this morning and my stomach is doing backflips. It was that cheap diner coffee, too. You know the place on 4th Street? The one with the neon sign that's always buzzing? The food's decent, I guess, if you like your eggs swimming in grease, but the coffee tastes like battery acid. The waitress there, Linda, she's been working there since I was a teenager. She’s got this hair that’s sprayed so stiff it looks like a helmet. I always wonder how long it takes her to do that in the morning. She must go through a can of hairspray a week...

Wait, sorry. The age thing. Yeah, before I was 12. Definitely. Teachers were always on my case about not sitting still and blurting things out way back in elementary school.
Have your symptoms, such as trouble paying attention or feeling restless, caused any significant problems for you at work, at home, or in your relationships?

Yeah, it's definitely causing issues. At work, it’s gotten serious enough that I’ve actually had formal warnings. I worry all the time that I could lose my job or, you know, cause a major safety problem on the line because I can't just stay at my station. 

Speaking of safety, corporate just sent down this new safety inspector last week. Guy walks around with a little tablet, wearing these brand-new, spotless steel-toed boots. You can just tell he’s never worked a day on the actual floor. He tried to make us switch to these new foam earplugs, but they expand way too much and make your ears itch like crazy. I wore them for half a shift and was digging at my ear so much it turned bright red. Kind of reminded me of when I got stung by a yellowjacket right on the earlobe at my cousin’s Fourth of July barbecue. My ear swelled up to the size of a golf ball. We were smoking ribs, and the sweet barbecue sauce must have brought the whole hive over...

Wait, sorry, I'm doing it again. Problems, right. So, work is pretty bad. And at home, it's tough too. My wife and kids get really frustrated with me. They have their schedules, but I just end up disrupting their routines instead of helping things run smoothly. 

Like, my wife will be trying to get the kids out the door for school, and I'll suddenly decide I need to reorganize the pantry right that second because I noticed the cereal boxes are crooked. We always buy those massive double-boxes of Cheerios from Costco. Man, have you seen the lines at Costco lately? It is an absolute zoo in there. Last time I went, I saw two people literally screaming at each other over a parking spot. A guy in a minivan and this lady in a Honda. I just parked way in the back by the tire center. I don't mind the walk, honestly, it gives me a reason to move around. Plus, I like looking at the tires they leave stacked up outside. I need new ones for my wife's car before winter hits...

But anyway, yeah. Work warnings, and messing up the family schedule. It's causing a lot of friction.
Have you ever been diagnosed with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder or anything similar by a healthcare professional?

Diagnosed? No, no doctor's ever told me I had anything like that. I actually try to avoid the doctor if I can, to be honest. The last time I even saw a healthcare professional was when I tweaked my shoulder on the assembly line a couple years back. The company made me go to this occupational health clinic over in the Westgate plaza. The waiting room chairs were those awful hard plastic ones that are bolted to the floor, you know? You can't even scoot them back to stretch your legs, which drove me crazy. 

I was sitting next to this guy who had a bandage wrapped all the way up his forearm, and he smelled strongly like turpentine. We got to talking, and it turns out he works at the commercial paint plant down by the river. You know that place? They had a massive spill there back in, what, 2008? Turned a whole mile of the riverbank neon green for a week. The local news anchors were out there in their rubber boots doing live shots every night. I remember watching it on the TV with my dad. My dad used to fish in that river all the time when I was a kid. He caught a catfish out of there once that was almost three feet long. Man, he had to practically wrestle that thing into the aluminum boat, and it snapped his favorite rod right in half. He was so mad about the rod he almost threw the fish back... 

Wait, sorry. A diagnosis. Right. No, I've never been diagnosed with anything like that. Nobody's ever brought it up before.
Have you experienced these symptoms, like trouble paying attention or feeling restless, in multiple settings, such as at work, at home, or in social situations?

Yeah, pretty much everywhere. Like I was saying, work and home are the big ones, but it's social stuff too. I can't even just sit and hang out normally. Like, I went over to my buddy Mike's house to watch the football game on Sunday. He just bought this massive 75-inch TV, the thing literally takes up his entire living room wall. But I couldn't even sit on the couch for more than a couple minutes. I kept getting up, pacing behind the couch, messing with his drink coasters. 

He collects these vintage beer coasters from all over the place. He's got one from a brewery in Germany that shut down like fifty years ago. He actually went to Germany back in his twenties, did a whole backpacking trip across Europe. I always wanted to do something like that, just take a train through the Alps. I saw a documentary on the History Channel about the Swiss railway system once, and the engineering is just unbelievable. The way they tunnel through solid granite... they use these massive tunnel boring machines. We use some heavy machinery on the production line, obviously, but nothing like that. Our main stamping press is loud enough to rattle your teeth, though. The concrete floor actually shakes every time it comes down. You get used to it after a few years, but the new guys always jump out of their skin the first time they hear it...

Wait, sorry, I lost track again. Multiple settings. Yeah, it's everywhere. Work, home, hanging out with friends. I just can't seem to turn the motor off, no matter where I am.
Have your symptoms affected your relationships with friends or caused problems in social situations?

I don't think so? I mean, I'm not really sure if it's caused actual problems. Like, I haven't noticed my friends getting really mad at me or cutting me off, if that's what you mean. Most of the guys I hang out with are just guys from the plant or buddies I've known since high school, so they're pretty used to how I am. 

Like Mike, we've known each other since tenth grade. We played on the varsity baseball team together. I was shortstop. Man, I loved playing infield, just always having to be ready for the ball. Our coach was this super intense guy, Mr. Henderson. He taught shop class too. He used to make us run foul poles until our lungs burned if we missed a sign from the dugout. He drove this beat-up old Ford Ranger that sounded exactly like a riding lawnmower. I'm not kidding, it was so loud. One time, the muffler completely rusted through and fell off while he was pulling over the speed bump in the school parking lot, and it just dragged and threw sparks all the way down the asphalt. The principal actually came running out of the front office waving his arms because he thought a car was on fire... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, problems with friends. Yeah, no, I haven't really noticed anything major like that. They just kind of ignore it when I get antsy.
Did you have trouble sitting still or paying attention when you were really young, like before you were 7 years old?

Yeah, definitely. I was like this even as a kid, way before middle school. My teachers were always moving my seat around because I just couldn't stay put. I was always blurting out answers before they even finished asking the question, and I'd get in trouble for butting into other kids' work. 

I remember my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable. She was this really strict lady who always wore these thick, knitted cardigans, even when it was hot out. She had this huge collection of ceramic owls on her desk. Like, dozens of them. Every time you walked past her desk, you had to be super careful not to bump into it, or all those little owls would rattle against each other. One time, Jimmy Peterson—he was this kid who always had a runny nose—he tripped over his own shoelaces and knocked one of the owls right off the edge. It shattered into a million pieces on the linoleum. Mrs. Gable turned so red I thought she was going to have a heart attack right there. Jimmy started crying, and then the school nurse had to come in. The nurse was always giving out those tiny paper cups of ginger ale if you said your stomach hurt. I used to fake a stomach ache just to get the ginger ale, but it was always flat...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, when I was young. Yeah, I was definitely hyper back then, getting into trouble for not sitting still and interrupting people.

Can you think of any specific instances or behaviors from when you were really little, like before you were 7 years old, that might have been related to your current troubles with restlessness or paying attention?

I mean, yeah, like I was just saying, it was definitely happening way back then. Even before middle school, honestly. I was always the kid who couldn't stay put. My teachers were constantly moving my seat around the classroom trying to find a spot where I wouldn't be a distraction. I was always blurting out answers before they even finished asking the question, and I'd get in trouble for butting into other kids' work.

Like, I remember this one time in first or second grade, we had these little cubbies where we kept our lunchboxes. Mine was this awesome metal Transformers one. It had Optimus Prime on the front. I loved that thing. I actually still have some of my old toys in a box in my attic. My mom saved them all. She kept everything, even my old Little League trophies. They're all dusty now, but it's cool to look at them sometimes. I found my old baseball glove up there last month when I was looking for the Christmas decorations. The leather was all dried out, though. You really have to oil those things if you want them to last. My dad taught me how to use neat's-foot oil on it when I was a kid. He was a mechanic, so he always had all sorts of oils and greases in the garage. His hands were permanently stained black from the engine grease. He used to use this orange pumice soap that smelled like fake oranges to scrub them clean every night...

Wait, sorry. I did it again, didn't I? Uh, what was the question? Specific things from when I was little? Yeah, just the seat moving, calling out answers, and getting into trouble for bothering the other kids while they were trying to work. It's always been like that.
Have you experienced trouble paying attention or feeling restless in quiet or low-stimulation environments, such as during meals or while watching TV?

Yeah, definitely. Like, if we're just sitting down for dinner or trying to watch TV, and I have to sit still, it feels like this crazy pressure building up inside my chest and my legs. Like I’ve got to move or do something right then and there or I’ll literally crawl out of my skin. My wife gets so annoyed because we'll be watching a movie, and I just can't stay on the couch. 

We were trying to watch this new WWII documentary the other night. I love history stuff, especially the planes. My grandfather flew a B-17 in the war. He actually brought back a piece of shrapnel that hit his wing. He kept it in this little wooden cigar box on his dresser. It was an old Swisher Sweets box. He used to smoke those on his back porch every Sunday afternoon. The smell of those things always reminds me of him. He had this old basset hound named Buster who would just lay there at his feet, snoring louder than a freight train. That dog was so lazy, he wouldn't even get up if you dropped a hot dog right next to his nose, he'd just kind of stretch his neck out to eat it... 

Wait, I'm off track again, aren't I? Sorry about that. What were you asking? Oh, quiet environments. Yeah, it's just that intense pressure where I feel like I have to move.
Did your trouble with paying attention and restlessness start before you were 12 years old?

Yeah, for sure. Like I mentioned before, this has been going on since I was really little, way before I was 12. Even before middle school, it was the exact same stuff. I could never just sit in my chair like a normal kid. The teachers were always shuffling my desk around to different corners of the room because I couldn't stay put. And I'd always just yell out the answers before they even finished asking, or I'd get in trouble for leaning over and messing with whatever the kid next to me was doing. 

I remember this one kid I always sat next to, Kevin. Kevin had this crazy collection of those little muscle men figures, you know, M.U.S.C.L.E. men? They were all pink and squishy. We used to try and trade them under the desk, but I'd always get too loud or drop them. Speaking of pink, my aunt had this completely pink bathroom. Pink tiles, pink sink, even pink toilet paper. I didn't even know they made pink toilet paper until I went to her house. She lived out in Ohio, near this huge cornfield. We used to drive out there every Thanksgiving in my dad's old station wagon. That car had the fake wood paneling on the sides and those rear-facing seats in the back. My sister and I would sit back there and make faces at the cars behind us until my dad would yell at us to knock it off. He had this really deep voice that would just boom through the car...

Uh, man, I'm doing it again. Sorry. My brain just goes. What did you ask? Before I was 12? Yeah, definitely. The seat moving, calling out, bothering other kids... it was all happening way back then.

We were trying to watch this new WWII documentary the other night. I love history stuff, especially the planes. My grandfather flew a B-17 in the war. He actually brought back a piece of shrapnel that hit his wing. He kept it in this little wooden cigar box on his dresser. It was an old Swisher Sweets box. He used to smoke those on his back porch every Sunday afternoon. The smell of those things always reminds me of him. He had this old basset hound named Buster who would just lay there at his feet, snoring louder than a freight train. That dog was so lazy, he wouldn't even get up if you dropped a hot dog right next to his nose, he'd just kind of stretch his neck out to eat it... 

Wait, I'm off track again, aren't I? Sorry about that. What were you asking? Oh, quiet environments. Yeah, it's just that intense pressure where I feel like I have to move.

doctor.intent: Determine if symptoms meet criteria for onset before age 12 for ADHD
doctor.question: Did your trouble with paying attention and restlessness start before you were 12 years old?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: I was like this even as a kid—teachers were always moving my seat because I couldn’t stay put, called out answers, and got into trouble for butting into other kids’ work before middle school.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the symptoms started before the age of 12, which directly matches the requirement for onset of symptoms prior to age 12.

patient.answer:
Yeah, for sure. Like I mentioned before, this has been going on since I was really little, way before I was 12. Even before middle school, it was the exact same stuff. I could never just sit in my chair like a normal kid. The teachers were always shuffling my desk around to different corners of the room because I couldn't stay put. And I'd always just yell out the answers before they even finished asking, or I'd get in trouble for leaning over and messing with whatever the kid next to me was doing. 

I remember this one kid I always sat next to, Kevin. Kevin had this crazy collection of those little muscle men figures, you know, M.U.S.C.L.E. men? They were all pink and squishy. We used to try and trade them under the desk, but I'd always get too loud or drop them. Speaking of pink, my aunt had this completely pink bathroom. Pink tiles, pink sink, even pink toilet paper. I didn't even know they made pink toilet paper until I went to her house. She lived out in Ohio, near this huge cornfield. We used to drive out there every Thanksgiving in my dad's old station wagon. That car had the fake wood paneling on the sides and those rear-facing seats in the back. My sister and I would sit back there and make faces at the cars behind us until my dad would yell at us to knock it off. He had this really deep voice that would just boom through the car...

Uh, man, I'm doing it again. Sorry. My brain just goes. What did you ask? Before I was 12? Yeah, definitely. The seat moving, calling out, bothering other kids... it was all happening way back then.
